chunks: I asked him about a man who said: 'If I marry so-and-so woman, then she is divorced; and if I buy so-and-so (slave), then he is free; and if I buy this cloth, then it is for the poor.'
So he said: 'It amounts to nothing. One cannot divorce except what one owns, and one cannot give in charity except from what one owns.'

key_terms.حُرّ: Free — the legal status of a slave who has been manumitted (itq)
key_terms.طَالِق: Divorced — the legal status of a woman whose husband has pronounced the formula of divorce (talaq) over her
key_terms.يَتَصَدَّق: He gives sadaqa — charitable donation as a form of voluntary piety
key_terms.يَمْلِك: He owns/possesses — legal ownership (milk) as the prerequisite for valid disposal
key_terms.يُطَلِّق: He divorces — pronouncing talaq, the Islamic formula of divorce

ai.seo_question: Can a man pronounce a conditional divorce before marriage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Qays narrates that he posed a legal question to Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the validity of conditional pre-emptive declarations — pledging divorce, manumission, or charitable donation contingent on future acquisitions. The Imam's ruling is clear and concise: such declarations are legally null and void. The ruling is grounded in the fundamental Islamic jurisprudential principle that legal acts (talaq, itq, sadaqa) require present ownership of the subject matter — one cannot validly dispose of what one does not yet own. This hadith forms part of the doctrinal basis in Shia fiqh for the invalidity of suspended divorce (talaq mu'allaq).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays,
(It has been narrated) Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who said, ‘I shall marry so and so woman, so she is divorced, and I shall buy so and so (slave) so he is free, and if I were to buy this cloth, so it is for the poor’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with anything. There is neither a divorce except what he owns, not a charity except with what he owns’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who says, ‘If I marry so and so woman she is divorced; if I buy so and so slave, he is free and if I buy this cloth it is for the destitute.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not have any valid effect; he cannot divorce until he is married and owns. He cannot give charity except what he owns.’”
